README:
One row per PHYSICAL BOOK on the shelf, and the only place a book is described. tools/series.py reads it; tools/fetch_puzzle.py --reindex copies the browser's half of it into puzzles/index.json, which is where app.js reads it. Nothing may hand-copy a row into either of those files: a shelf label spelled in two places is how the eighteen-key BOOK_SHELF object in app.js and the `shelf` column in tools/series.py came to be two copies of one fact.

book_index IS THE PUZZLE NUMBER'S HIGH HALF and is NEVER REUSED. A puzzle's stored number is book_index * 1000 + its position in the book, so book 17's twenty-third puzzle is book-17023. Retiring a book leaves its index retired with it: reusing one would silently point a saved grid, a vote and an indexed URL at another book's crossword.

volume IS THE NUMBER THE BOOK PRINTS ON ITSELF, not its place in this file. Twenty-eight of the thirty were read off a cover scan; morse and brainsharp print no number anywhere and their volumes are invented, which tools/data/book_acquisition_plan.json says in those words. Two publishers' volume 2 are different books, which is why the volume is never the key.

shelf, kind and name all have the volume written into them by the accessors in tools/series.py, never here twice over: shelf + volume is what a reader sees beside a position ("Penguin book 5 No 18"), kind + volume + " Cryptic" is the noun on the crawlable page, and name + " No <position>" is the puzzle's title.

EVERY SHELF NAMES ITS OWN BOOK. The homepage list prints shelf with no badge beside it — one pill covers the whole shelf now — so a bare "book 2" would be the Herald's, the Scotsman's, the Sunday Telegraph's and the Daily Mail's at once.

`was` is the per-book series key these puzzles were filed under until 2026-09-19, and it is load-bearing rather than historical: /puzzles/penguin-5018/ and /puzzles/penguin5-18/ are indexed, shared and hold saved progress, and tools/series.py builds both of those old ids out of this field so they keep resolving.

A book is registered here BEFORE its scan is read — tools/acquire_book.py refuses an identifier this file does not carry, so a run cites the book it actually read or does not run.

published IS THE YEAR THE BOOK'S IMPRINT PAGE PRINTS ("First published ... 1995", or the copyright year where it prints no "first published" line), as a four-digit string. It is every one of the book's puzzles' `date`: the filer writes it, and tools/puzzle_integrity.py flags a book puzzle whose date differs. A year and not a day, because no imprint prints a day; archive.org's own metadata is no substitute, since it gives "June 1999" for all five Penguin Guardian volumes.
